# Machine-file (`.mach`) format v2 fixtures

## Provenance

**Every file here was produced by the Tamga API's own encoder**, not by this
SDK and not by hand. They were generated by calling
`tamga-api`'s `src/shared/crypto/machine_file.rs::encode_machine_file` — the
exact function that serves `POST /v1/accounts/{a}/machines/{m}/actions/check-out`
— over a representative `{"data": <MachineResource>, "meta": <LicenseFileClaims>}`
payload, with the signing keys generated per scheme and the matching public key
recorded in `manifest.json`.

Do not regenerate these from this crate, and do not hand-edit them. A fixture
built by the code under test only proves the verifier agrees with itself. That
is precisely how the three defects this directory exists to catch survived: each
SDK tested against a file reproducing its own misreading of the format, CI stayed
green, and nothing the server actually emitted could be opened. If a case is
missing, it has to come from the server's encoder.

## What the fixtures pin down

| Property | Why a self-generated fixture would have missed it |
| --- | --- |
| `alg` carries a mandatory `+v2` marker (`base64+ed25519+v2`) | A verifier that compares the whole post-`+` remainder against the signing suffix rejects every real file. |
| Signing suffixes contain hyphens (`rsa-pss-sha256`, `ecdsa-p256`) next to an encoding prefix that also does (`aes-256-gcm`) | A parser that splits on the wrong delimiter, or takes a fixed segment index, passes on `ed25519` and fails here. |
| Encrypted `enc` is `"<nonce_b64>.<cipher_b64>"` — two **separately** base64'd halves | The server's own doc comment claims `base64(nonce‖ciphertext‖tag)` and is wrong; every SDK implemented the comment. Both halves are separately padded to a multiple of four, so a *lenient* decoder skips the `.` and reconstructs the right bytes by accident — Rust's strict engine does not, which is why the failure is visible here and latent elsewhere. |
| `rsa-sha256` is emitted for **both** `RSA_2048_PKCS1_SIGN` and `RSA_2048_JWT_RS256` | The file's `alg` cannot identify the scheme, so the caller-supplied scheme has to stay authoritative and `alg` a cross-check only. |
| The signed payload carries `meta` (`iat`/`exp`/`jti`/`kid`) | Without a real payload there is nothing to enforce `exp` against, and an expired machine file verifies forever. |

## `manifest.json`

A JSON object keyed by fixture name. The tests in
`tests/machine_file_v2_fixtures.rs` **iterate this manifest** rather than naming
files, so dropping in new fixtures plus their manifest entries extends coverage
with no test edit.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `file` | File name inside this directory. Defaults to `<name>.machine`. |
| `alg` | The `alg` string inside the certificate, asserted verbatim. |
| `encrypted` | Whether `enc` is AES-256-GCM sealed. |
| `enc_is_dot_separated` | Whether `enc` is `"<nonce_b64>.<cipher_b64>"`. Tracks `encrypted`. |
| `public_key_b64` | Base64 of the raw public key for `scheme`, exactly as `tamga-api`'s `extract_public_key` returns it: 32 raw bytes for Ed25519, a 65-byte uncompressed point for ECDSA P-256, DER `RSAPublicKey` for either RSA variant. |
| `kid` | Expected `meta.kid` — the server's short digest of the account's public key. |
| `license_key` | HKDF input material for an encrypted file; `null` for a plain one. |
| `fingerprint` | The machine fingerprint; HKDF `info`, and the expected `data.attributes.fingerprint`. |
| `expired` | Whether `meta.exp` is already past at the file's own `meta.iat`. |
| `scheme` | The governing licence's signing scheme. Accepted either as the wire spelling (`ED25519_SIGN`) or the Rust variant name (`Ed25519Sign`). |

## Time handling

These are captured artefacts, so their `meta.exp` is fixed and every one of them
is expired against today's wall clock. The tests therefore evaluate each fixture
at a caller-supplied timestamp via
`tamga::checkout::machine_file::verify_machine_file_at`, using the file's own
`meta.iat` as "now". That keeps the expired/not-expired split meaningful and the
suite deterministic no matter when it runs.
